source: typesafe-changelog (reading under review: .agi/context/local-maxxing/troves/2026-09-19-cua/read-typesafe-changelog.json, 23492 bytes, written 2026-09-18 20:27). Reviewer re-opened 7 cited sources on 2026-09-18/19: docs.typesafe.ai/models.md, /sdk/python/changelog.md, /sdk/javascript/changelog.md, /llms.txt, /api.md, /model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md, /cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md, plus typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev and evals.typesafe.ai/{agent_trace_observability,security_incidents}, and local acts_replay.md, cua_trace_excerpt.json, cua_trajectory_mapping.md, json_cache/*.json. Payload IS schema-valid (all 7 required keys present) and the data is largely clean: I re-verified ~20 quoted numbers and found ZERO fabricated figures. The failures below are framing, internal contradictions, and over-claimed seeds, not invented data. Verified-good spot checks: jev-1.13.0 + $42/$0.042 + 250k tok/s + 1200 req/min + 64k/32k context + both aliases (models.md); Python v0.7.0 2026-09-18 msgspec->pydantic + response_model + str-subclass fix, v0.6.0 2026-09-15 Score.criteria dict->sequence, v0.5.7 2026-09-14 (python changelog); JS v0.6.0 2026-09-15, v0.5.7 2026-09-11, no v0.7.0 (js changelog); 90.8% raw / 99.2% policy / 25.8% uncertain / 74.2% automatic / mean prob std 0.0098 / max 0.0515 / 114 ms / $0.000046 / 0.60 gate (choice cookbook); Noul answer has NO confidence while Choice+Score do (api.md); structural invariant noul 0.72 + not-noul 0.47 = 1.19 and 'score levels are weak in numerical calibration' (jaggedness, last reviewed 2026-09-17); 193.6x/444.6x + average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 + the OpenAI/Anthropic bias caveat (launch blog); evals rows 71.6%/$0.0003/0.5s and 61.7%/$0.0001/0.3s (evals pages); no model-changelog page in llms.txt and parallel_questions 12.2x/10.0x (llms.txt).
unsupported_claims: SUMMARY says 'TypeSafe is stateless, streams nothing, batches nothing, and exports nothing.' 'Batches nothing' is CONTRADICTED by the source's own index: docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt (read 2026-09-18) describes cookbooks/parallel_questions.md verbatim as 'batching every question into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster with no change in answers', and the API's `questions` field is a map (api.md) designed for the docs' 'Speculative fan-out' pattern. The reading lists that exact batching fact in its own key_facts, so the summary contradicts its own body. Correct claim: no asynchronous batch ENDPOINT, but a single request natively batches many questions.

'The API call shape is unchanged since launch' (summary) is an UNVERIFIED inference from ONE api.md snapshot (2026-09-18) with no launch-era request example; the launch blog shows no raw HTTP shape. It is also in tension with the SDK v0.6.0 breaking change 'accept Score.criteria as an ordered sequence instead of a dictionary keyed by integers' (python changelog, 2026-09-15) -- whether the WIRE shape moved is exactly what was not checked. Tag it ESTIMATE, not established fact.

The launch blog is tagged 'dated 2026-09-14' (MEASURED) in key_facts, but the fetched page carries no visible publication date -- only author 'Diogo Almeida, founder, TypeSafe' (typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev, read 2026-09-18). If the date came from sitemap.xml that provenance is not stated; as written the tag overstates the evidence. Downgrade to unverified.

reusable_assets calls the Choice self-consistency cookbook 'Directly reusable as the town's calibration harness' and the summary calls it 'The most relevant published calibration artifact'. The cookbook is n=1 document (one borderline moderation post, 8 questions, 15 repeats) and its own text says 'These percentages measure repeatability only ... None of this shows accuracy or superiority' (consistency_choice_cookbook.md, MEASURED). Generalising it to a town-wide calibration harness is unsupported by n=1; the reading's open_questions admits the n=1 limit but the summary and asset list do not carry the caveat.

'stateless' and 'streams nothing' rest on absence-of-evidence in api.md, not on any statement in models.md or api.md that the service keeps no state or offers no stream. That is a legitimate negative finding but should be phrased as 'no streaming endpoint documented', not as a property guarantee.

seed #1 claim 'round-trips without loss of the Choice/Noul/Score shape' is CONTRADICTED by the repo artefact the seed cites as its target: .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trajectory_mapping.md (read 2026-09-18) says 'The reverse direction is also lossy' and marks `answers` as 'GAP-as-ANSWER' (cua carries raw DOM+screenshot, not a typed answer) and `act` identity as a GAP that must be minted. 'Round-trips without loss' is the opposite of what the mapping doc measured.

seed #2 calls the Agent Trace Observability input schema 'a superset of the CUA trajectory export fields'. The ATO input requires instructions, every conversation turn, each tool call with args+result, a final message, and customer feedback (evals.typesafe.ai/agent_trace_observability, MEASURED); the on-box CUA trace has only event_name/data_json/data_images/trajectory_id/timestamp with no conversation, no final message, no feedback, no model (cua_trace_excerpt.json, MEASURED). ATO is a richer DIFFERENT shape, not a superset; the seed's own falsifier concedes this, so the claim is likely false before it is run.
errors_found: Internal contradiction: summary 'batches nothing' vs the reading's own key_fact 'batching 13 questions into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster' (both in the same JSON). One of them is wrong; the key_fact is the verified one (llms.txt, 2026-09-18).

seed #4 ('Pinning jev-1.13.0 and logging response.model is necessary for reproducibility') is already implemented and measured: acts_replay.md (MEASURED) records 'MODEL=jev-1.13.0 (pinned)' and 'response model id jev-1.13.0 on every call'. The seed therefore returns ~0 new knowledge, and its 'falsifier' is not falsifiable as written ('a release changes the alias while the versioned id remains pinnable (which is the point)') -- it restates the claim instead of naming a breaking observation.

Agent Trace Observability outcome count: the reading asserts '7 typed outcomes'. The page renders 'AUTO-CLOSE NOT A BUG HUMAN REVIEW PRIORITY REVIEW FILE ISSUE · ROUTE PAGE ON-CALL' (MEASURED), where the middle dot could be read as one 'FILE ISSUE · ROUTE' outcome (6) or two (7). The assertion is plausible but the ambiguity is unflagged.

The jev-1.13 failure-mode list is reproduced faithfully, but the reading omits the page's #9 'Generation' failure mode ('Jev is not trained to generate text ... this will not work well and will be very slow', jaggedness 2026-09-17). For a town that wants small models generating coupled-oscillator maps, the explicit no-generation limit is the single most load-bearing omission.

The reading never notes that `confidence` is 'derived from probabilities' (api.md, MEASURED). It is therefore redundant with the top probability, not an independent calibration channel -- which is why the choice cookbook thresholds on top probability (0.60), not on confidence. Presenting confidence as a first-class field without this note invites the town to treat a derived quantity as new signal.

Not an error but a provenance gap: every URL in the reading is a live page; no source is pinned to a commit/version or archived. Given the demonstrated SDK churn (three Python releases in four elapsed days), unpinned doc claims can silently change, and the reading's own parallel-questions figure moved between its 09-17 and 09-18 reads (11.5x/9.6x -> 12.2x/10.0x) -- it correctly flags that, but does not apply the lesson to its other numbers.
missing_angles: SDE cascade cookbook (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md, listed in llms.txt 2026-09-18): 'Uses a 2-stage structured-data-extraction cascade (mini -> verify -> reasoning) to get most of the quality of a big reasoning model at a fraction of the cost.' This is a direct instantiation of the town's vision 3 (two or more tiny models cooperating) and a CPU-cheap pipeline; the reader never mentions it. Highest-value missed angle.

Hierarchical classification (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): classifies deep patent/retail/biomedical/source-code hierarchies 'using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities' -- a CPU-feasible decision search that maps onto the town's head-pruning / coupled-map generation threads.

classification_using_confidence (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md): 'read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it' -- the confidence-as-routing pattern the town needs, unexamined by the reader.

Re-ranking (top-1 5%->18%, top-10 38%->62%), semantic_find (218 line ids scored in one request), autoformat (two-request structure recovery), pre-parsed value extraction -- all CPU-only retrieval/extraction/formatting uses of a tiny decision model, all listed in llms.txt, none cited. These map directly to the town's 'efficient inference on lighter hardware' vision.

The 64k/32k state cap interaction with CUA is never stated as a bound. The town's replay averaged 4906 input tokens/act (acts_replay.md, MEASURED), but the local CUA trace excerpt carries 16,477-16,496 HTML bytes per observation and a full 252K-char trace (cua_trace_excerpt.json, MEASURED). A raw CUA trajectory cannot fit the 32k-token state budget, so seeds #1/#2 must filter/chunk before any jev call -- a hard feasibility constraint on the reader's two headline interop seeds.

The owner's 'qwen3.8 50b' id resolution and the recurrent/looped-transformer + KV-cache threads are untouched. This source may be out of scope, but the reader's reusable_assets claim to serve the town's CUA work while never connecting to the town's stated model line.

No independent check that the reading's 'no model changelog' conclusion is not just absence in one index: GET /v1/models release_date is the one probe that would settle it, and the reading lists it as an open question rather than stating that the conclusion is an absence-of-evidence result (a key would be needed, so correctly not attempted, but the epistemic status should be explicit).
strongest_seed: seed #3 -- 'The 0.60 top-probability uncertain gate transfers to the town's q1 verdict-class decision.' Highest knowledge-per-token on CPU: $0 (the cache exists and provably holds q1 choice probabilities + confidence -- MEASURED .agi/context/local-maxxing/typesafe/json_cache/001b81d27fa6e031e9a05f99.json: q1 probabilities {inconclusive_lean_proved 0.5, disproved 0.15, inconclusive_lean_disproved 0.29, pending 0.05, proved 0.01}), ~10 min, a pre-registered falsifier (policy agreement > 0.85, automatic coverage not below ~50%), and it targets the town's actual measured failure (q1 raw 0.743, ECE 0.196, falsifier tripped -- acts_replay.md, MEASURED). MANDATORY caveat to attach before running: q1 is leakage-contaminated (1094 of 1473 corpus node bodies, 74%, literally contain their own verdict word -- acts_replay.md), so a 0.60 gate may simply abstain on the hard/leaky cases and report a repeatability artifact as a calibration win. The experiment must report abstention rate and policy agreement conditioned on leakage, or it is not knowledge.
weakest_seed: seed #4 -- 'Pinning jev-1.13.0 and logging response.model is necessary for reproducibility.' Already implemented and measured (acts_replay.md: MODEL=jev-1.13.0 pinned, response model jev-1.13.0 on all 1110 calls), so it yields ~0 new knowledge; its stated falsifier is a tautology rather than a breaking observation. Next weakest is seed #2, whose central 'ATO is a superset' claim is contradicted by the on-box trace's missing conversation/final-message/feedback fields before any experiment is run.
